newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy MIF dealers to be able to act on own account.
newsitem.headline: Italy MIF dealers to be able to act on own account.

text.p: The 90 dealers on the Italian bond futures market (MIF) will from May be able to quote prices directly for deals on their own account, the bond market (MTS) and futures market management committee decided on Tuesday.
Market sources said the decision was aimed at boosting the Italian derivatives market which is dwarfed by London's LIFFE. In 1996, trading on MIF was around 20 percent down on 1995.
On the MTS secondary government bond market, automatic matching will be introduced in May or June whereby an operator, unlike currently, will not know the name of his counterparty.
There are also plans to trade a one-month RIBOR future, a repo and stripped coupon market. In 1996, MTS trading rose 28 percent.
The MTS-MIF management committee also announced at today's members' annual meeting the aim to transform the two markets into SpAs, or joint stock companies, over the next three to four months.
The Treasury has already approved the plan which envisages stakes to be open also to non-members of the two markets.
